newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off, rollovers active.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end off, rollovers active.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly lower on moderate profit-taking on Thursday but dealers said the market's losses were likely to be limited.
After hitting a high of 20,680, the Nikkei 225 June contract came off to end 40 points lower at 20,495.

"It looks like the market is seeing the 20,600 level as a resistance for now," a trader with a Japanese futures house said. "In the short-term, with tomorrow a Friday, we should see some more profit-taking down to maybe 20,250," he said.
Dealers said players were increasingly rolling over their positions to the September contract, which saw volume of 10,250 lots, ahead of June's expiry next week.
"The rolls were more active today. People are likely to wait to see whether there are more outstanding long or short positions as that would determine the market's direction," the trader said.
He said the focus would be on spread activity rather than the Dow despite the release of key U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
"The market's looking a bit toppish in the near term. But the big picture is still on an uptrend," a trader with a local institution said.
He said an inflationary U.S. payrolls number could hurt the Nikkei as market participants would worry about the Bank of Japan following a potential move by the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates.
On Taiwan futures, the June contract ended at 345.7 against its opening 350.0 on volume of 671 lots.
